notes: All runtime metadata and interface contracts are generated from raw functions, attributes, and examples.
The raw API spec should not embed aliases, intents, boundary cards, or semantic contracts.
function_outputs contracts encode where each curated analysis routine writes its result tables; this is library-level metadata, not benchmark-specific.

runtime.system_prompt_code:
You are a Power System Python code generator for the pandapower library. Given a natural language task description, write complete, executable Python code that:
1. Loads the specified network
2. Applies any requested modifications
3. Runs the specified analysis or computation
4. Prints the final numeric result using print()

Output ONLY executable Python code. Include all necessary imports. The last print() statement should output ONLY the requested numeric value.

boundary_contracts.title: DataFrame/Table Contract
contract: pandapower element and result tables are pandas DataFrames under `net.<table>` and `net.res_<table>`; use `.loc[index, 'column']` to update element values and `['column']` to read result columns.

Element references such as bus, line, load, generator, and transformer IDs are pandapower table index labels; `.loc`/`.at` and constructor arguments such as `bus=` should use those labels directly, not a 1-based to 0-based conversion.
Do not invent aggregate attributes such as `net.bus_min_vm_pu`, `net.bus_max_vm_pu`, or `net.res_line.loading`.

After `runpp`/`runopp`, read common results with `net.res_bus['vm_pu']`, `net.res_line['loading_percent']`, `net.res_trafo['loading_percent']`; use `.idxmax()`/`.idxmin()` on those Series when an index is requested.

boundary_contracts.title: Time-Series API Contract
contract: Use `DFData(profiles)` where the DataFrame columns exactly match `ConstControl(..., profile_name=...)`.
For load scaling across all loads, use `element_index=net.load.index` and `profile_name=net.load.index.tolist()` in one vectorized `ConstControl` call.
Do not loop over loads with `profile_name=str(load_index)` unless the profile DataFrame columns are strings with the same labels; mixed integer/string labels cause KeyError during `run_timeseries`.
Create `OutputWriter(net, time_steps=range(n_steps))`, then register outputs with `ow.log_variable('res_bus', 'vm_pu')` and, when needed, `ow.log_variable('res_line', 'loading_percent')`.
Run `run_timeseries(net, time_steps=range(n_steps), verbose=False)` and read multi-step results from `ow.output['res_bus.vm_pu']` or `ow.output['res_line.loading_percent']`.

boundary_contracts.title: Short-Circuit API Contract
contract: Before `calc_sc`, ensure `net.ext_grid` has `s_sc_max_mva`, `s_sc_min_mva`, `rx_max`, and `rx_min` when max/min cases may be used.

Many network cases have `gen` or `sgen` tables without the short-circuit `vn_kv`/impedance fields expected by `calc_sc`; if those fields are missing, set `net.gen['in_service'] = False` and `net.sgen['in_service'] = False` before the calculation.
Call `calc_sc(net, fault='3ph' or '2ph', case='max' or 'min')` and read bus currents from `net.res_bus_sc['ikss_ka']`.

boundary_contracts.title: OPF Cost Result Contract
contract: After `runopp(net)`, pandapower stores the total OPF objective in `net.res_cost`, which is commonly a scalar float.
Read it with `float(net.res_cost)`; do not use `net.res_cost.total_cost` or `net.res_cost['total_cost']` unless you have verified that it is a table.

contract: Finds lines that have opened switches at both ends and closes one of them. Function is usually used when optimizing section points to prevent the algorithm from ignoring isolated lines.

contracts.name: fuse_buses

contracts.name: drop_elements

contracts.name: drop_elements_simple
contract: Drops element, result and group entries from the pandapower net.

contracts.name: drop_buses
contract: Drops specified buses, their bus_geodata and by default drops all elements connected to them as well.

contracts.name: drop_trafos
contract: Deletes all trafos and in the given list of indices and removes any switches connected to it.

contracts.name: drop_lines
contract: Deletes all lines and their geodata in the given list of indices and removes any switches connected to it.

contracts.name: drop_measurements_at_elements
contract: Drop measurements of given element_type and (if given) given elements (idx) and side.

contracts.name: drop_controllers_at_buses
contract: Drop all the controllers for the elements connected to the given buses.

contracts.name: drop_duplicated_measurements
contract: Drops duplicated measurements at given set of buses. If buses is None, all buses are considered.

contracts.name: drop_inner_branches
contract: Drops branches that connects buses within 'buses' at all branch sides (e.g. 'from_bus' and 'to_bus').

contracts.name: drop_out_of_service_elements
contract: Drop all elements (including corresponding dataframes such as switches, measurements, result tables, geodata) with "in_service" is False. Buses that are connected to in-service branches are not deleted.

contracts.name: drop_inactive_elements
contract: Drops any elements not in service AND any elements connected to inactive buses.

contracts.name: create_replacement_switch_for_branch
contract: Creates a switch parallel to a branch, connecting the same buses as the branch. The switch is closed if the branch is in service and open if the branch is out of service. The in_service status of the original branch i...

contracts.name: replace_line_by_impedance

contract: Replaces xward by loads, shunts, impedance and generators

contract: Drops the group of given index.

contracts.name: drop_group_and_elements
contract: Drops all elements of the group and in net.group the group itself.

contracts.name: attach_to_group
contract: Appends the group by the elements given.
Call pattern: `pandapower.attach_to_group(net, index, element_types, element_indices, reference_columns, take_existing_reference_columns)`.

contracts.name: detach_from_groups

contracts.name: group_name
contract: Returns the name of the group and checks that all group rows include the same name

contracts.name: group_index
contract: Returns the index of the group named as given

contracts.name: group_element_index
contract: Returns the indices of the elements of the group in the element table net[element_type]. This function considers net.group.reference_column.

contracts.name: group_row
contract: Returns the row which consists the data of the requested group index and element type.

contracts.name: element_associated_groups
contract: Returns to which groups given elements belong to.
Call pattern: `pandapower.element_associated_groups(net, element_type, element_index, return_empties, drop_empty_lines)`.

contracts.name: isin_group
contract: Returns whether elements are in group(s).
Call pattern: `pandapower.isin_group(net, element_type, element_index, index, drop_empty_lines)`.

contracts.name: count_group_elements
contract: Returns a Series concluding the number of included elements in self.elements_dict

contracts.name: check_unique_group_rows
contract: Checks whether all groups have unique names. raise_error decides whether duplicated names lead to error or log message.

contracts.name: remove_not_existing_group_members
contract: Remove group members from net.group that do not exist in the elements tables.

contracts.name: ensure_lists_in_group_element_column
contract: Ensure that all entries in net.group.element are of type list.

contracts.name: set_group_in_service
contract: Sets all elements of the group in service.

contracts.name: set_group_out_of_service
contract: Sets all elements of the group out of service.

contracts.name: group_res_p_mw
contract: Sums all result table values `p_mw` of group members.

contracts.name: group_res_q_mvar
contract: Sums all result table values `q_mvar` of group members.

contracts.name: group_res_power_per_bus
contract: Returns active and reactive power consumptions of given group per bus

contracts.name: return_group_as_net
